activities.topic: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence and Smart Systems

activity_1.title: Find Smart Technology Around You
steps: Look around your house or village.
Identify three devices that behave in a smart way.
Observe how these devices help people perform tasks easily.
Think about how they assist in decision-making.

activity_2.title: Notice Smart Suggestions
steps: Use a mobile phone, TV, or video platform.
Observe the suggestions shown after watching content.
Notice how similar videos or songs are recommended.
Think about how the device learns your preferences.

activity_3.title: Pattern Finding Game
steps: Ask a family member to show five similar objects.
Observe the objects carefully.
Identify patterns such as color, shape, and size.
Relate this to how AI learns from patterns.

extra_exploration.task: Ask where machines are becoming smarter.

think_and_notice: Which device in your house seems the smartest?
How do you think machines learn what people like?
Why should we use technology responsibly and carefully?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your ideas with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize AI in everyday life
learning_outcomes.description: Students identify smart technologies used in daily activities.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand the concept of pattern recognition
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how similarities and patterns help in learning.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop curiosity about emerging technologies
learning_outcomes.description: Students begin asking questions about intelligent systems.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect technology with real-life applications
learning_outcomes.description: Students relate AI concepts to devices used in their environment.

bonus_activity: Think about one problem around your house that technology could solve.
Examples: automatic lights, farming reminders, weather alerts
Imagine how AI could help create such solutions.

activities.topic: Prompting and Clear Instructions in AI

activity_1.title: Give Instructions to a Family Member
steps: Ask a family member or friend to draw something.
First give unclear instructions and observe the result.
Then give clear and detailed instructions.
Compare both results and observe the difference.
examples: Clear: Draw a small house with two windows and a tree next to it.

activity_2.title: Describe an Object Clearly
steps: Choose an object in your house.
Describe the object without showing it.
Include details like color, shape, size, and use.
Ask someone to guess the object.

activity_3.title: Follow Clear vs Unclear Directions
steps: Ask someone to give you directions to find an object.
Follow unclear directions first.
Then follow clear directions.
Compare how easy or difficult each was.
examples: Unclear: Look somewhere in the room.
Clear: Look on the table near the window.

extra_exploration.task: Find situations where clear instructions are important.

think_and_notice: What happened when the instructions were unclear?
How did the result change when the instructions were detailed?
Why do machines like AI need clear prompts?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand the importance of clear instructions
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how clarity improves task outcomes.

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize the role of prompts in AI
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand that AI depends on human instructions.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop communication and reasoning skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students practice describing objects and instructions clearly.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect AI concepts with real-life communication
learning_outcomes.description: Students relate prompt design with everyday instructions.

bonus_activity: Ask a simple question to an AI tool or search engine.
Example: Tell me about animals.
Then ask a more detailed question: Explain how lions hunt in simple words for children.
Observe how better questions give better answers.

activities.topic: Creativity, Imagination, and Descriptive Prompting in AI

activity_1.title: Imagine a Creative Object
steps: Think of one unusual or funny object by combining two different things.
Describe your idea in one or two clear sentences.

activity_2.title: Draw Your Idea
steps: Draw the imagined object in your notebook.
Add details such as colors, background, and actions.
Focus on expressing your idea rather than making a perfect drawing.

activity_3.title: Describe Your Drawing
steps: Show your drawing to a family member.
Describe what the object is, where it is, and what it is doing.
Check if they understand your idea clearly.

extra_exploration.task: Find one real object that could be improved using imagination.
examples: Water bottle that reminds you to drink water

think_and_notice: Was it easier to imagine or draw your idea?
Did your family member understand your idea when you described it clearly?
Why does AI need clear descriptions to generate images?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your answers with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop creative thinking
learning_outcomes.description: Students imagine new objects by combining ideas.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand the role of descriptive prompts
learning_outcomes.description: Students learn that clear descriptions lead to better results.

learning_outcomes.title: Improve visual communication skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students express ideas through drawings and explanations.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect AI creativity with human imagination
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand that AI tools create images based on human prompts.

bonus_activity: Ask a family member what they would design using AI.
Examples: smart farming machines, creative buildings, new types of vehicles
Think about how AI tools could help visualize such ideas.

activities.topic: Pattern Recognition and Visual Understanding in AI

activity_1.title: Quick Drawing Challenge
steps: Ask a family member or friend to give you an object name.
Draw the object within 20 seconds.
Repeat this activity three times with different objects.
Observe how quickly you can recognize and draw common shapes.

activity_2.title: Guess the Drawing
steps: Ask a family member to draw something in your notebook.
Try to guess what they are drawing before they finish.
Observe how quickly you can recognize the drawing.

activity_3.title: Make Your Drawing Alive
steps: Draw a simple character.
Imagine how the character would move.
Think about actions like walking, jumping, or dancing.
Relate this to how AI can convert drawings into animations.

extra_exploration.task: Find three objects that can be represented using simple shapes.

think_and_notice: Was it easy to guess the drawing quickly?
Which objects were harder to recognize from drawings?
Why does AI need many examples to recognize drawings correctly?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your answers with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand pattern recognition
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how shapes help identify objects.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop visual and creative thinking
learning_outcomes.description: Students create drawings and imagine movement or actions.

learning_outcomes.title: Improve observation and communication skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students practice guessing and explaining drawings.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect AI concepts with real-life activities
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how AI recognizes images and patterns.

bonus_activity: Draw three simple emojis in your notebook.
Examples: happy face, sad face, surprised face
Ask someone to guess the emotion and think about how AI recognizes emotions from images.

activity_1.title: Create a Simple Song
steps: Think of a small topic and create a 4–5 line song.
Write your song in Marathi, Hindi, or English.
Focus on expressing your idea clearly.
examples: Example: My school is bright and fun, We learn and play in the sun.

activity_2.title: Add Rhythm
steps: Sing your song with a rhythm.
Clap your hands or tap the table while singing.
Observe how rhythm makes the song more engaging.

activity_3.title: Imagine an Album Cover
steps: Draw a picture that represents your song.
Use symbols or scenes related to your topic.
Relate this to how AI tools generate images from ideas.
examples: Birthday cake for a birthday song
School building for a school song
Clouds and rain for a rain song

extra_exploration.task: Listen to a song at home and identify its theme and type.
examples: Identify what the song is about
Recognize the type of music (happy, calm, fast)

think_and_notice: Was it easy or difficult to write your own song?
How did rhythm or clapping change the song?
How could AI help people create music quickly?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your answers with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop creative expression
learning_outcomes.description: Students create songs using their own ideas.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand the connection between words and music
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how rhythm and lyrics form a song.

learning_outcomes.title: Improve artistic imagination
learning_outcomes.description: Students visualize music through drawings.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect AI tools with human creativity
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how AI can generate music and art from prompts.

bonus_activity: Ask a family member what kind of song they would create using AI.
Examples: farming life, village festivals, friendship
Think about how AI music tools could generate such songs automatically.

activities.topic: Voice Recognition and Sound Processing in AI

activity_1.title: Speak and Write
steps: Ask a family member to say three short sentences aloud.
Listen carefully to each sentence.
Write the sentences in your notebook.
Observe how spoken words become written information.
examples: The sun rises in the east.

activity_2.title: Change Your Voice
steps: Speak the same sentence in different ways.
Try a happy voice, a serious voice, and a funny voice.
Notice how tone and pitch change the sound.
examples: My name is ______ spoken in different tones

activity_3.title: Identify Sounds Around You
steps: Sit quietly for 2–3 minutes.
Listen carefully to your surroundings.
Write down five different sounds you hear.
Observe how sounds help you understand your environment.

extra_exploration.task: Ask how mobile phones understand voice commands.

think_and_notice: Was it easy or difficult to write sentences by listening?
How did the voice change when you spoke differently?
Why do machines need voice recognition systems?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your answers with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand speech communication
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how spoken language conveys information.

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize voice variations
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how tone and pitch change the meaning of speech.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop listening and observation skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students identify sounds and speech in their environment.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect AI voice systems with real-life communication
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how AI converts speech to text and text to speech.

bonus_activity: Try giving a simple voice command to a device if available.
Examples: Call Mom, Play music
Observe how the device understands and responds to voice commands.

activities.topic: AI Avatars, Storytelling, and Human Expression

activity_1.title: Tell a Short Story
steps: Think of a short story with 3–4 sentences.
Tell the story aloud to a family member.
Use voice and expressions to make the story interesting.
Observe how storytelling becomes engaging with expression.
examples: A small robot wanted to learn farming. One day it helped a farmer water the plants. The plants grew quickly, and the farmer was happy.

activity_2.title: Act Like a Character
steps: Choose a simple character.
Speak one sentence as that character.
Change your voice and expression to match the role.
Observe how voice affects character identity.
examples: Robot: I am a robot learning to grow plants.

activity_3.title: Create a Talking Picture
steps: Draw a simple character in your notebook.
Write one sentence that the character will speak.
Imagine how the character would talk in a video.
Relate this to how AI avatars create talking animations.
examples: This robot helps farmers grow healthy crops.

extra_exploration.task: Watch a short video and observe human expressions and storytelling.
examples: Understand how the story is explained

think_and_notice: Did the story become more interesting when spoken with expression?
How did changing your voice or character affect the story?
Why do AI avatar videos use voice and facial expressions?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your answers with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand storytelling and communication
learning_outcomes.description: Students learn how voice and expressions convey messages.

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize digital avatars and AI video concepts
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how AI can turn text and images into talking characters.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop creative expression
learning_outcomes.description: Students create characters and simple stories.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect AI video tools with real-life communication
learning_outcomes.description: Students relate avatar videos to human storytelling methods.

bonus_activity: Look at a photo in your house and imagine what the person might say.
Think about what voice they would have.
Write one sentence that the photo might speak.

activity_1.title: Observe a Photo Carefully
steps: Take a photo from your home such as a family photo or a poster.
Look carefully at the image.
Identify the main object (foreground).
Identify the background.
Write your observations in your notebook.

activity_2.title: Imagine Changing the Background
steps: Look at the same photo.
Imagine placing the main object in a different background.
Think about how the scene would look.
Relate this to AI tools that change backgrounds automatically.
examples: Person in room imagined on a beach

activity_3.title: Remove an Object (Imagination Exercise)
steps: Observe the photo again.
Imagine removing one object from the image.
Think about how the image would change.
Draw the scene without that object in your notebook.
examples: Remove a tree from the background
Remove a chair from a room
Remove a vehicle from a road scene

extra_exploration.task: Find situations where photo editing is useful.

think_and_notice: Which part of the photo was the main focus?
How did the image look when you imagined a new background?
Why are AI tools useful for editing photos quickly?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your answers with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand foreground and background in images
learning_outcomes.description: Students identify the main subject and surrounding elements in a picture.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop visual observation skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze objects and details in images.

learning_outcomes.title: Improve creative thinking
learning_outcomes.description: Students imagine different backgrounds or edits for images.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect AI image editing with real-world uses
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how AI tools help modify and enhance photos.

bonus_activity: Look at a poster or advertisement at home.
Identify the main object, background design, and colors used.
Think about how AI tools might have helped create or edit the image.

activities.topic: Visual Storytelling and AI Scene Generation

activity_1.title: Imagine a Scene
steps: Think of a short movie-like scene.
Write 2–3 sentences describing the scene.
Focus on characters, actions, and surroundings.
examples: A robot helping farmers in a field
A flying car above a city
A dinosaur walking in a village
A dog wearing sunglasses on a beach
Example: A robot is watering plants in a green farm while the sun is shining.

activity_2.title: Draw the Scene
steps: Draw the scene in your notebook.
Include main characters, background, and actions.
Focus on expressing your imagination rather than perfection.

activity_3.title: Turn Your Scene into a Story
steps: Write 3–4 lines explaining what happens next.
Describe actions and outcomes in the scene.
Relate this to how AI generates videos or stories from ideas.
examples: The robot helps the farmer water crops.
Soon the plants grow healthy and strong.

extra_exploration.task: Find a place around you that could become a movie scene.

think_and_notice: Was it easier to imagine or draw the scene?
How did adding details improve your scene?
Why do AI tools need detailed prompts to generate images or videos?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your ideas with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop visual imagination
learning_outcomes.description: Students imagine scenes and convert them into drawings.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand prompt-based generation
learning_outcomes.description: Students learn that clear descriptions help create better visual results.

learning_outcomes.title: Improve storytelling skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students explain events and actions in a scene.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect AI creative tools with human imagination
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how AI can generate images and videos from ideas.

bonus_activity: Watch a short video or movie clip.
Observe background, characters, and actions.
Think about how AI tools could create similar scenes automatically.
